title: Autoreconcile Terraform module for private EKS control plane provisioning and rolling upgrades
creator: Aisha Kumar
description: Build a reusable Terraform module to provision Redwood Private control plane clusters (AWS EKS) that is idempotent, supports safe rolling upgrades of nodegroups and control-plane-affecting resources, and includes built-in health checks and an optional reconcile mechanism to remediate drift. The module should support private endpoint-only clusters, cross-account KMS keys for secrets, and hooks for our upgrade orchestration. Scope excludes on-prem Kubernetes distributions (separate work).
acceptance_criteria: Module can create and destroy a private EKS cluster and nodegroups in a repeatable, idempotent way with Terraform 1.5+
Built-in preflight validations run and fail-fast on missing networking/KMS/IAM prerequisites
Rolling upgrade workflow is supported: new nodegroup creation -> cordon/drain -> nodegroup deletion without service downtime for typical Redwood workloads
Health checks export metrics to CloudWatch (or Prometheus) and emit events to Console tracing for failed post-upgrade validations
Optional autoreconcile (Lambda or controller) can be enabled to detect drift in critical resources and either attempt automated repairs or create actionable incidents in Ops
Module documentation and usage examples in the repo + Terraform registry entry
E2E test in CI (github-actions) that exercises create/upgrade/destroy with acceptance smoke tests passing
implementation_notes: Primary implementation in Terraform with a module interface that accepts existing VPC/subnets or will create the VPC when requested
Use aws_eks_cluster, aws_eks_node_group and aws_eks_addon resources; avoid inline null_resource long-running provisioners except where strictly necessary for validation
Support blue/green style nodegroup upgrades by provisioning replacement nodegroups with unique names and switching workloads via kubectl drain in CI-driven runbooks

Provide a lightweight reconcile path: optional AWS Lambda + EventBridge rule that runs terraform plan/apply using a locked state or triggers the infra-tooling pipeline. The reconcile flow is gated by feature flag to prevent surprise writes in production
Expose outputs for cluster endpoint, kubeconfig data, OIDC URL, IAM role ARNs, and KMS key alias used for secret encryption
Add guardrails: timeouts, max_unavailable for rolling operations, and automated rollback markers in S3 to allow safe undo
Make module testable: include a minimal example/fixture and a longer integration test that runs in ephemeral accounts in CI
Prioritize least-privilege IAM roles and require security_review_required=true for any change to kms/cross-account roles
